claims.statement: A sparse subset of specific attention heads and MLP components jointly implements the minimal propositional-logic reasoning task — the circuit is small relative to the full model (target |shortlist|/|total| ≤ ~15% with completeness ≥ 0.9 and single-removal minimality drop ≥ 0.05 on Mistral-7B).

data.source: synthetic propositional-logic template (facts + rules + query) — parameterised by k, chain-length, lexicon; anchor cell (k=3, chain=2, natural), corrupt_fact corruption

claims.method: Attribution-patching screen (Attribution Patching) — rank attention heads + MLPs by causal contribution to logit-diff on clean vs corrupt_fact, shortlist by cumulative-effect + 15% size cap; completeness = restore-with-shortlist LD-recovery; minimality = avg single-component-removal LD-drop (M1)

main_experiment.key_stats: shortlist_size=158, sparsity_fraction=0.150, cumulative_effect=0.758, completeness_LD=0.955 ✓, completeness_PD=0.905, minimality_avg=0.0014 ✗ (target ≥0.05), minimality_median=0.0027
main_experiment.headline: 158-component shortlist (15.0% of components — at the size cap) recovers 0.955 of clean-vs-corrupt logit-diff (completeness ✓), but single-component removal drops recovery by only 0.0014 on average (minimality ≪ 0.05 target ✗) — heavy pairwise redundancy in the large shortlist

claims.statement: The circuit decomposes into a small number of modular sub-circuits with distinct functional roles (fact-identification, rule-application, answer-projection) rather than presenting as an entangled mixture — target role-assignment matrix S with per-component dominance ratio ≥ 2×, dissociation ≥ 0.1, Jaccard cross-cell stability ≥ 0.6, null-shuffle p ≤ 0.01.

data.source: synthetic propositional-logic template — role-specific corruptions (corrupt_fact / corrupt_rule / corrupt_answer / corrupt_neutral) at anchor cell + stability cells (k=5,chain=2) and (k=3,chain=3)
data.used_n: 300 pairs × 3 roles (M4) + 200 pairs × 3 roles × 2 cells (M4.stab); top-40 shortlist (17 attn + 23 mlp)
data.subset_note: top-40 shortlist used (not full 158) — justified by M2 dose-response: top-31 already recovers 0.946 of causal effect; documented in EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md

claims.method: Role-dissociation via type-specific counterfactual corruption + null-shuffle p-value test; per-component dominance ratio + role-partition dissociation; cross-cell Jaccard stability across (k=5,chain=2) and (k=3,chain=3) (M4 + M4.stab)

claims.statement: Activation-patching / causal-mediation experiments show that the identified components are both necessary (clean→corrupt patching restores correct behaviour) and sufficient (their outputs alone drive the answer) — target recovery ≥ 0.8 on {logit_diff, prob_diff, KL} with matched-control specificity gap ≥ 0.6.

data.source: synthetic propositional-logic template — anchor cell (k=3, chain=2, natural), 500 clean + 500 matched-corrupt pairs per corruption type
data.used_n: 500 anchor pairs (M2 necessity + M3 sufficiency); 5 seeds for sufficiency

claims.method: Path-patching necessity (clean→corrupt patch shortlist; measure LD/PD/KL recovery + matched-control specificity, M2) + Sufficiency reinsertion (corrupt+identified-component-clean-patch; resample-ablate everything else; 5 seeds, M3) + Cross-family verify on Gemma-2-9B (M5)

main_experiment.key_stats: necessity: LD_recovery=0.955 ✓, PD_recovery=0.905, specificity_gap=0.836 ✓; sufficiency: LD_recovery=0.113 ✗ (target ≥0.8), PD_recovery=0.116, KL_recovery=0.076, matched-control ≈0, specificity_gap=0.113, per-seed std=0.036; cross-family Gemma-2-9B: necessity LD=1.018 ✓, sufficiency LD=0.019 ✗
main_experiment.headline: circuit is *necessary but not sufficient* — path-patching restores 0.955 clean-vs-corrupt LD with specificity_gap 0.836 (necessity ✓), but reinserting only shortlist activations while resample-ablating the rest recovers only 0.113 (sufficiency ✗, stable across 5 seeds); the same necessity-yes/sufficiency-no pattern recurs on Gemma-2-9B — a cross-family robust negative on the sufficiency half

iteration.narrowed_to: the identified circuit is necessary but not sufficient (a partial refutation of the strong claim); the necessary half is cross-family robust (Mistral-7B & Gemma-2-9B)

claims.final_status: ✓ verify PASS (robustness=1.0) — the necessary-but-not-sufficient asymmetry is cross-family robust; the sufficiency half of the given claim is refuted, the necessity half stands (narrative caveats added by iteration ⓪)
caveats: KL recovery denominator collapses (tiny baseline KL(clean||corrupt)=0.043) — LD and PD are the definitive metrics

figures.caption: C3 — necessary-but-not-sufficient asymmetry, cross-family robust. On Mistral-7B and Gemma-2-9B, path-patching restores logit-diff (necessity ✓, 0.955 and 1.018); reinserting the shortlist while resample-ablating the rest recovers almost nothing (sufficiency ✗, 0.113 and 0.019).
